Posterior probability of a favorable value of an endpoint

Source: R/PosteriorProb.R
PosteriorProb.Rd

Computes the posterior probability that a response rate, a survival probability or a hazard ratio is favorable: above (or below) a target value for one group, or better than in a reference group by a margin.

Usage

PosteriorProb(
  measure = c("rate", "surv", "hr"),
  a,
  b,
  target,
  time = NULL,
  a.ref = NULL,
  b.ref = NULL,
  higher.better = TRUE,
  n.nodes = 200
)

Arguments

measure

"rate", "surv" or "hr".

a, b

Parameters of the posterior distribution: beta shape parameters for "rate", gamma shape and rate of the hazard for "surv" and "hr". Positive numeric vectors.

target

Target value of the rate or of the survival probability without a reference group; margin of the difference, or bound of the hazard ratio, with a reference group.

time

Time of the survival probability, required for measure = "surv".

a.ref, b.ref

Parameters of the posterior distribution of the reference group, or NULL for a one-sample probability.

higher.better

Logical: TRUE if higher rates or survival probabilities (longer times) are favorable.

n.nodes

Number of Gauss-Legendre nodes for the probability of a difference.

Value

Numeric vector of posterior probabilities. a, b, target, time, a.ref and b.ref are recycled to a common length.

Details

The posterior distributions are given by their parameters.

  • measure = "rate": the rate p has a beta posterior with shape parameters a and b, for example a = a0 + x and b = b0 + n - x for x responders among n patients and a Beta(a0, b0) prior.

  • measure = "surv": the event times are exponential with hazard lambda, which has a gamma posterior with shape a and rate b, for example a = a0 + d and b = b0 + T for d events and total follow-up time T and a Gamma(a0, b0) prior. The parameter is the survival probability S(time) = exp(-lambda * time).

  • measure = "hr": the hazard ratio lambda / lambda_ref of two such exponential models; a reference group is required.

Without a reference group (a.ref and b.ref are NULL), the result is P(p >= target) or P(S(time) >= target) when higher.better = TRUE, and P(p <= target) or P(S(time) <= target) otherwise.

With a reference group, the result is P(theta - theta_ref >= target) when higher.better = TRUE and P(theta - theta_ref <= target) otherwise, where theta is the rate or the survival probability and target is a margin in (-1, 1). For the hazard ratio, the result is P(lambda / lambda_ref <= target) when higher.better = TRUE (longer times are favorable) and P(lambda / lambda_ref >= target) otherwise. The two posterior distributions are independent.

One-sample probabilities and the probability of the hazard ratio are computed in closed form (beta, gamma and F distributions). The probability of a difference is a one-dimensional integral computed with an n.nodes-point Gauss-Legendre rule on the probability scale of one of the two posterior distributions; with the default 200 nodes the absolute error is of the order of 1e-6 or smaller.

References

Chakraborty, S., Dubey, A. K., Kumar, A. and Chan, I. (2026). A two-stage dose optimization framework for oncology drug development with multiple efficacy and safety endpoints via an integrated benefit-risk assessment. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, published online. doi:10.1080/19466315.2026.2668381

See also

BenefitRisk

Examples

# P(ORR >= 0.3) with 18 responders among 40 patients and a Beta(0.5, 0.5) prior
PosteriorProb("rate", a = 0.5 + 18, b = 0.5 + 22, target = 0.3)
#> [1] 0.9780309

# P(S(6) >= 0.5) with 20 events in 300 months of follow-up
PosteriorProb("surv", a = 0.5 + 20, b = 300, target = 0.5, time = 6)
#> [1] 0.996266

# P(AE rate - AE rate of the reference <= 0.1)
PosteriorProb("rate", a = 0.5 + 12, b = 0.5 + 28, target = 0.1,
              a.ref = 0.5 + 8, b.ref = 0.5 + 32, higher.better = FALSE)
#> [1] 0.5094168

# P(HR <= 0.8)
PosteriorProb("hr", a = 0.5 + 20, b = 300, target = 0.8,
              a.ref = 0.5 + 25, b.ref = 280)
#> [1] 0.5893727
